hero.body:
The Fort Pierce City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney while the city searches for a permanent replacement, following the departure of the city's top legal staff. The city commission decided not to renew City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract. Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman has resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month.

Commissioner Michael Broderick, who voted against Wallace's appointment, said the departures come as Fort Pierce faces several significant development decisions. Broderick pointed specifically to future development proposals on South Hutchinson Island, including potential changes to the South Beach Overlay, a zoning regulation that currently limits building heights and density. He said removing those restrictions could clear the way for much taller development on the island. Broderick told CBS12 News the city has no independent legal representation to deal with several volatile projects slated to come before the city commission in short order.

Wallace previously worked in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager. Supporters of the appointment said that experience makes her well-positioned to step into the role and help keep city business moving while a search gets underway. Broderick said the commission appointed the assistant city manager to be a charter officer in the city, which he said reeks of duplicity and multiple bosses to report to.

The commission approved a contract with executive search firm S. Rene Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney. The agreement authorizes up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. City officials expect the interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution. The search for a permanent city attorney is expected to continue over the coming months.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce City Commission voted 3-2 this week to appoint Deputy City Manager Camille Wallace as interim city attorney, capping a complete turnover of the city's legal department just as several high-profile development decisions are expected to reach commissioners. City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract was not renewed, Assistant City Attorney Felicia Holloman resigned, and temporary attorney Caroline Valentin is set to leave at the end of the month. The transition has raised questions about who will guide the city through development proposals on South Hutchinson Island and potential changes to the South Beach Overlay, a zoning regulation that currently limits building heights and density.

Commissioner Michael Broderick voted against Wallace's appointment and objected to what he described as a conflict of interest. "So what the city commission did against my protests is they appointed the assistant city manager to now be a charter officer in the city of Fort Pierce," Broderick said. "In my opinion, that reeks of duplicity and multiple bosses you need to report to. I'm not sure how that is even possible to do." Broderick told CBS12 News the city has no independent legal representation to handle volatile projects slated to come before the commission.

Broderick pointed specifically to future development proposals on South Hutchinson Island. He said removing South Beach Overlay restrictions could clear the way for much taller development on the island. "There are several very volatile projects that are slated to come in front of the city commission in short order, and we really have no independent legal representation to be able to deal with that on behalf of the city commission, in my opinion," Broderick said.

Supporters of Wallace's appointment said her experience working in the City Attorney's Office before becoming deputy city manager makes her well-positioned to provide continuity while the city loses much of its legal staff. The commission also approved a contract with executive search firm S. Renée Narloch & Associates to recruit a permanent city attorney, authorizing up to nearly $31,000 in fees and expenses for the search process. City officials expect the interim appointment to return to the commission in the form of a formal contract and resolution.
